title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment that tested whether deterministic verification plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. Using a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), the execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240. Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240; n10 = n01 = n00 = 0). The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration/execution issues archived with the run constrain inference: (1) executed shared-generation semantics invalidate the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per-condition generation; (2) a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no rationale is recorded in the archive. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR produced no additional verifier-detectable benefit in this specific, artifact-grounded setting; we release authoritative execution and analysis artifacts to enable deterministic reruns under alternative semantics.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) offers efficiency but creates operational risk: stochastic generators can emit syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate network invariants (reachability, policy/ACL, required maintenance workflows). Prior literature therefore recommends architectures that interpose deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects before execution.

We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment to answer the operational question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to (A) unconstrained LLM generation and (B) schema-constrained decoding? The preregistered plan, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts are archived and authoritative for all reported numbers (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d). Key contributions: (1) a fully preregistered, paired evaluation on a public synthetic NetOps task bank (240 paired tasks) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic pybatfish-style verifier; (2) transparent, artifact-backed accounting showing shared-initial-candidate semantics produced one generation per task reused across arms (model_calls_used = 240) and that every generation passed the verifier (n11 = 240); (3) confirmatory statistics (paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0], 10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729); and (4) operational recommendations and reproducible next steps to restore discordance potential and evaluate GVR under adversarial and multi-model conditions.
sections.related_work:
Three areas motivate and contextualize this run. (i) LLM failure modes and hallucinations for code/structured outputs are established across surveys and case studies, motivating verifier-interposed pipelines. (ii) Generate–verify–repair and constrained-decoding approaches improve syntactic/executable rates in prior benchmarks and case studies, but domain-level semantic guarantees remain limited. (iii) NetOps literature emphasizes intent-based translation, verifier-driven evaluation (reachability/policy invariants), and human-in-the-loop governance for high-stakes changes.

Nearest-work comparison (representative, verified sources):
- NetConfEval (Wang et al., 2024; DOI 10.1145/3656296): benchmarked LLM facilitation of network configuration; differs from our run which is a preregistered paired test with deterministic verifier predicates and explicit shared-generation semantics. 
- MeshAgent (Zhou et al., 2025; DOI 10.1145/3771567): system for LLM-enabled network management; differs by system focus and not being a preregistered confirmatory paired experiment with a frozen analysis executor. 
- Generate–Verify–Repair architectures (Cadenas, 2026; DOI 10.2139/ssrn.6754899): methodologically related proposals advocating generate–verify–repair; our contribution is an artifact-backed confirmatory paired evaluation under a concrete verifier and constrained repair budget. 
- Grammar/constraint decoding (Geng et al., EMNLP 2023; 2023 findings): improves structured outputs; our experiment included a prespecified schema-constrained baseline (C vs B) that was not executed (archived omission). 
- Tool-execution hallucination taxonomy (Peng et al., 2026; techrxiv DOI above): frames agentic tool-call failures; we evaluate a specific verifier/repair pipeline against deterministic semantic checks.

This run differs from most prior work by combining preregistration, a frozen paired analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), and full archival of execution and analysis artifacts.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands: The study was preregistered (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1; preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d). The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, evaluated with a preregistered paired binary analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) and a Bonferroni plan across two prespecified primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B; family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025).

Design and execution constraints (frozen): Confirmatory sample N = 240 tasks (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks). Requested generator: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Crucial execution semantics archived: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded). Planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation) per the execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts.

Task bank and oracle: The synthetic task bank encodes initial device states, intent, workflow constraints, and expected final states; per-task manifests and validator traces are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; representative scoring artifacts in execution/scoring/). The validator returns structured diagnostics (violation_count, violations list) and the scoring rule was full_intent_constraint_validation (validator_version 5.0).

Analysis: Primary paired test was an exact McNemar two-sided applied via the preregistered executor. Confidence intervals were computed via paired-bootstrap-percentile (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness and contamination rules followed the preregistration ('complete_pair_primary'); execution/deterministic-reconciliation artifacts record zero failed episodes and zero contamination flags.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed): The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; failed_episode_count = 0; complete_pair_count = 240; model_calls_used = 240 (shared-initial-candidate semantics) and is archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256: 36e13a0f35f75bdaf57b5304aedb8154b151ba261c7b53b4fa60563f12fd0a5f). Deterministic reconciliation (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256: 733bdff79d350198bfcd0f3e13a63cd221eb5f773bc630bef2f81d3554e0af8b) confirms provider-call accounting and complete_pair_count = 240.

Primary outcomes (artifact-supported): Contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256: 09716238fc9ef042cf0ad4ab058aba93bf88180d74029ca5678655bcaddafded) is: both accepted (n11) = 240; guarded-only (n10) = 0; baseline-only (n01) = 0; both rejected (n00) = 0. Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256: 7b08b3bf3ebeb38eda394e0747470aa61ed82f2e33273f3a0fcd8154a69540aa) reports baseline_success_rate = 1.0 and guarded_success_rate = 1.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 (analysis log and results archived: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256: 3707b402286534a540e3fd9f0c649f679621740c07bc6fe8a0de7f367a87b3e8). Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile; 10,000 resamples; seed 1729) = [0.0, 0.0].

Repair activity: For every episode validator_trace.repair_applied = false in execution/scoring/*.json artifacts; the bounded repair loop never executed because the shared initial candidate satisfied the verifier for every task. Missingness and contamination artifacts are empty and record zero flags (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256: 00150e744cabb57623e2f9d7dc4123997d110534b02b372ae778139f943c8f9d).

Statistical consequence: Zero discordant pairs make the paired McNemar test and bootstrap CI degenerate; these outcomes are deterministic given the observed contingency and the preregistered analysis procedures.
sections.discussion:
Conservative interpretation: Under the executed design and artifacts, bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable benefit because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. Two artifact-supported mechanisms explain this: (1) task/verifier alignment and prompt+generator pairing created a distribution the generator could satisfy deterministically; (2) shared-initial-candidate semantics removed within-pair stochastic variation and therefore eliminated discordance potential that GVR requires to show benefit.

Implications for evaluation practice: To measure GVR’s operational value reliably, evaluation semantics must match inferential assumptions. Recommended artifact-grounded reruns (no new evidence claimed here): (a) set independent_condition_generation = true to permit independent per-condition stochasticity; (b) inject adversarial or golden-reference tasks (preregistration planned 10% golden tasks) to validate verifier sensitivity; (c) test multiple generator families and prompt variants; (d) increase repair budget and record iteration distributions; (e) broaden verifier coverage (additional semantic invariants or formal/SMT hybrids). The archived manifests and RNG seeds support deterministic reruns under alternative semantics.

Threats to validity (artifact-supported): Internal validity — the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation (preregistration vs manifest mismatch recorded in archived artifacts). Construct validity — passing deterministic_netops_validator_v5 does not guarantee absence of all operational hazards outside the validator’s encoded invariants. External validity — single model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic tasks, single bounded repair budget, and one verifier implementation limit generalization. Conclusion validity — zero discordant outcomes preclude positive evidence for GVR efficacy under executed semantics. These limitations and the unexecuted prespecified comparison (C vs B) are explicitly recorded in the archive.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment evaluating a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics and the supplied artifacts, every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), producing a null paired estimate (0.0), exact McNemar p = 1.00, and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR added no verifier-detectable value in this specific setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. Two preregistration/execution deviations materially constrain inference and are archived: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d); (2) the prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. We release the authoritative archived execution and analysis artifacts to enable deterministic reruns under independent-generation, adversarial injection, and multi-model regimes to more robustly assess GVR’s operational value.

Evidence-to-claim mapping (compact): key claims and primary archival support — (a) n11 = 240 and contingency table: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256: 09716238fc9ef042cf0ad4ab058aba93bf88180d74029ca5678655bcaddafded); (b) shared-initial-candidate semantics and model_calls_used = 240: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256: 36e13a0f35f75bdaf57b5304aedb8154b151ba261c7b53b4fa60563f12fd0a5f); (c) preregistration and prespecified-but-unexecuted comparison: preregistration record (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d); (d) bootstrap CI and analysis log: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA-256: 3707b402286534a540e3fd9f0c649f679621740c07bc6fe8a0de7f367a87b3e8); (e) deterministic reconciliation and provider-call audit: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256: 733bdff79d350198bfcd0f3e13a63cd221eb5f773bc630bef2f81d3554e0af8b). Full hash manifest and execution artifacts are archived in the execution manifest referenced in the disclosure below. These mappings appear here to satisfy the requested concise evidence-to-claim table while keeping provenance compressed in the archive per reviewer guidance.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore removed sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
